newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRANCE EASES PAYROLL TAX TO KEEP STAR PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRANCE EASES PAYROLL TAX TO KEEP STAR PLAYERS.

text.p: French soccer players are to be given the same tax status as movie stars in a drive to halt their emigration to lower-tax countries, the government decided on Wednesday.

Alarmed by the exodus in recent years of more than 40 top footballers including Eric Cantona, David Ginola and French national captain Didier Deschamps, the cabinet approved a bill to give sports clubs relief on payroll taxes for professional players.

Under the new rules, 80 percent of players' earning will be considered to be royalties for the use of their image rather than a salary, and thus not subject to employers' social security levies which amount to about 55 percent of gross pay.

"By making possible a reduction in social charges on part of their income, this should enable high-level sportsmen to stay in our beautiful country and sportsmen from neighbouring European countries...to be attracted once again to our country," government spokesman Alain Lamassoure told reporters.
He said the cost to the public purse would be negligeable.
French soccer clubs had complained they could not afford to retain the country's best players, or sign foreign stars, because of the prohibitive cost of payroll taxes.
